images.title: Three layers of nine make 27
images.purpose: Shows a cube of edge 3 built from 3 separated layers of 3 by 3 unit cubes, 27 unit cubes in all.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One cube in a simple oblique view in the centre, its layers lifted slightly apart, with short labels to the right.
images.exact_structure: A cube of edge 3 unit cubes drawn in flat oblique view, split into exactly 3 horizontal layers stacked with small even gaps between them. Each layer is a 3 by 3 slab of exactly 9 equal unit cubes with visible edges. The bottom two layers are filled teal (#0072B2) and the top layer amber (#E69F00), 27 unit cubes in all. To the right: 3 layers, 9 per layer and, below them, 3³ = 27. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A cube of edge n is n layers of n × n unit cubes, so n³ in all.
images.description: Shows a cube of edge 3 built from 3 separated layers of 3 by 3 unit cubes, 27 unit cubes in all.

image_decisions.why: The tool's core move is stacking layers of unit cubes and reading the total as the cube.
